moved.sentence: **Break up long tasks** — split work > 50ms into smaller chunks so the main thread can paint and handle input between them.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the > 50ms threshold and the paint-and-handle-input reason.

moved.sentence: **Yield to the main thread.** Prefer `scheduler.yield()` where available — note it is **Chromium-supported but NOT yet Baseline** as of 2026 (limited availability).

judged.note: Both halves kept at SHOULD across two rules, including the Chromium-supported-but-not-Baseline-as-of-2026 caveat.

moved.sentence: Provide a fallback: feature-detect and degrade to `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r))` (loses the prioritized continuation) or the `scheduler-polyfill`.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with feature detection, the setTimeout degrade (and its lost prioritized continuation) and the scheduler-polyfill alternative.

moved.sentence: **Move heavy computation to a Web Worker** (parsing, diffing, crypto, image work) to keep the main thread free for rendering and input.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the four example workloads and the keep-the-main-thread-free reason.

moved.sentence: **Avoid layout thrashing** — batch DOM reads then writes; never interleave reads/writes in a loop that forces synchronous reflow.

judged.note: Avoid layout thrashing and batch reads-then-writes kept at SHOULD, and the 'never interleave' clause is kept as a MUST NOT.

moved.sentence: **Keep the DOM small** — oversized DOM trees (thousands of nodes) inflate style/layout cost on every interaction.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the thousands-of-nodes example and the style/layout-cost reason.
Kept at SHOULD in should-keep-dom-small: virtualize long lists.

moved.sentence: **Defer non-critical work** to idle time (`requestIdleCallback`) or post-interaction.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with both targets: idle time via requestIdleCallback, or post-interaction.

moved.sentence: **LCP**: preload the LCP image/font, serve responsive images, avoid render-blocking CSS/JS, use `fetchpriority="high"` on the hero image, and prefer server-side rendering for above-the-fold content.

judged.note: All five LCP quick wins are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **CLS**: reserve space for media and dynamic content; avoid inserting content above existing content; use `font-display: optional`/`swap` deliberately and preload fonts to reduce reflow.

judged.note: All CLS quick wins are kept at SHOULD, including deliberate font-display use and font preloading.

moved.sentence: Collect field data via the **`web-vitals` JavaScript library** (reports LCP, INP, CLS using the attribution build for debugging) or the Chrome User Experience Report (CrUX).

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with both sources (web-vitals library with attribution build, or CrUX).

moved.sentence: Wire a CI gate such as **Lighthouse CI** (`lhci autorun`) with assertions on metric thresholds and resource/byte budgets defined in a `budget.json`.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with Lighthouse CI, metric-threshold assertions and budget.json resource/byte budgets.

moved.sentence: Express budgets as concrete limits (e.g., total JS transfer <= 170KB compressed for the critical path) and fail the build on regression — this turns performance into a `tight-feedback-loop` and a `support-automation` boundary rather than a manual review step.

judged.note: Kept at SHOULD with the 170KB example, fail-on-regression and the tight-feedback-loop / support-automation reason.

moved.sentence: Treating Core Web Vitals as a deliberate, budgeted constraint (not an after-the-fact audit) is the durable practice; specific thresholds are reviewed periodically by the Chrome team, so pin to the dated thresholds above and re-verify against `web.dev/articles/vitals/`.

judged.note: Kept: the budgeted-constraint framing, the periodic-review reason and the pin-and-re-verify instruction at SHOULD; the dated thresholds it points to remain in the three-core-web-vitals part.
